problem.title: First and Last Refill per Patient
problem.prompt: A pharmacy runs a 90-day adherence program tracking patient refills. Write a query that returns one row per patient showing their patient_id, the medication name from their FIRST refill (earliest refill_date), and the medication name from their LAST refill (most recent refill_date) in the program. Use FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE window functions. Remember: to get the true last value in a partition, you must specify `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING` in your window frame, otherwise LAST_VALUE defaults to the current row. Order the final result by patient_id ascending. Note: some patients may have only one refill, in which case first and last medication will be the same.
problem.schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE refills (
  refill_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  patient_id INT NOT NULL,
  medication_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  refill_date DATE NOT NULL,
  days_supply INT NOT NULL
);
problem.example_input_data:
INSERT INTO refills (patient_id, medication_name, refill_date, days_supply) VALUES
(101, 'Lisinopril 10mg', '2024-01-15', 30),
(101, 'Metformin 500mg', '2024-02-20', 90),
(101, 'Atorvastatin 20mg', '2024-03-10', 30),
(102, 'Levothyroxine 50mcg', '2024-01-22', 60),
(102, 'Omeprazole 20mg', '2024-03-15', 30),
(103, 'Amlodipine 5mg', '2024-02-01', 90),
(104, 'Sertraline 50mg', '2024-01-10', 30),
(104, 'Sertraline 50mg', '2024-02-12', 30);

composite_moves: window FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY refill_date) with explicit frame for LAST_VALUE
deduplicate with DISTINCT or GROUP BY to one row per patient

hints: You need to use window functions to find the medication name from the earliest and latest refill for each patient.

FIRST_VALUE works as expected with the default frame, but LAST_VALUE requires you to specify `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING` to get the actual last value in the partition instead of just the current row.

After computing FIRST_VALUE and LAST_VALUE for every row, use DISTINCT or wrap in a subquery and GROUP BY patient_id to collapse to one row per patient. The window functions will produce the same first/last values for all rows in each patient's partition.
problem.answer_key:
SELECT DISTINCT
  patient_id,
  FIRST_VALUE(medication_name) OVER (
    PARTITION BY patient_id 
    ORDER BY refill_date
  ) AS first_medication,
  LAST_VALUE(medication_name) OVER (
    PARTITION BY patient_id 
    ORDER BY refill_date
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING
  ) AS last_medication
FROM refills
ORDER BY patient_id;

_meta.scenario: a prescription refill adherence program tracking 30/60/90 day refill rates

user_solution:
/*
SELECT t.*,
       FIRST_VALUE(val) OVER (PARTITION BY k ORDER BY ts
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS first_val,
       LAST_VALUE(val)  OVER (PARTITION BY k ORDER BY ts
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_val
FROM tbl t;
-- the explicit frame is required, or LAST_VALUE returns the current row
*/

SELECT DISTINCT
    patient_id,
    FIRST_VALUE(medication_name) OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY refill_date
               ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS first_medication,
    LAST_VALUE(medication_name) OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY refill_date
               ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_medication
FROM refills
ORDER BY patient_id;
